facts.raw_span: A 66-year-old female patient with osteoporosis presented with complaints of back pain
The pain was radiating to the left side and gradually worsening in recent months
The back pain had not improved despite left nephrectomy due to kidney stones about 1 year ago
The patient was taking alendronate 70 mg once a week for osteoporosis
Family history was unremarkable
mild left costovertebral angle tenderness
negative babinski sign and normal deep tendon reflexes on both lower limbs
neither sensory loss nor motor neurologic deficit
Comprehensive laboratory investigations including serum creatinine, calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone, thyrotropin and thyroid hormones were normal
Lumbar spine X-ray: Demonstrated degenerative changes of the vertebral bodies
Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry: T-scores of both the lumbar spine and proximal femur were less than -3
A 35 × 9 mm sized mass occupying the spinal canal at T8-T9 level

support_spans: A 35 × 9 mm sized mass occupying the spinal canal at T8-T9 level
Well-circumscribed intradural extramedullary lesion, hypointense on T1-weighted images and heterogene hyperintense on T2-weighted images
concepts.why: The presence of a well-circumscribed intradural extramedullary lesion with characteristic imaging features and positive staining for protein S-100 is unusual and points towards Schwannoma

support_spans: The lesion compressing the spinal cord from posterior showed peripheral rim enhancement around the central cystic area after contrast media injection
contradict_spans: Neoplastic cells were negative for epithelial membrane antigen
concepts.why: The presence of a lesion with peripheral rim enhancement and a central cystic area is unusual and could be seen in Meningioma, although the negative staining for epithelial membrane antigen makes it less likely
